quiet.title: Why this address's flood record is quiet
quiet.origin: Our counts of NWS flood reports near this address and across sampled places
quiet.text: No flood report within 5 km of this address is in our records. The closest flood report we could place was 9.0 km away, in 2023 (METZGER). We measured 25500 random places across the 51 states we have indexed: 71% had no flood report within 5 km, 29% had more than this address and 71% had the same number. A flood report exists only if someone filed one, and this is a count of reports we could place near an address. A quiet record means no report was filed close by. It does not mean nothing happened here, and it does not mean flooding is impossible.
quiet.quote: Heavy rains around 1 inch in a half hour to an hour resulted in Ash Creek in southwest Portland to over flow. Around 14 homes had varying amounts of flooding.

SE-961302.title: Excessive Heat, Jun 26, 2021
SE-961302.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-961302.text: Excessive Heat on Jun 26, 2021 in Greater Portland Metro Area (forecast zone ORZ006, YOUR zone: the address is inside it). Deaths: 93. Injuries: 0. Recorded damage: $100,000.
SE-961302.quote: Record breaking temperatures for 3 days in a row. Portland International recorded high temperatures of 108, 112, and 116 F (breaking its previous all time record of 107), and low temperatures of 70, 73, and 75 F. The Oregon State Police and Oregon Medical Examiner reported 67 deaths in Multnomah County from the heat, but it is suspected this fatality count is closer to 71. There were also reports of roads buckling due to heat. Cooling shelters were opened and many businesses closed and events postponed.

sentences.text: The most significant event in the record for this area was the Excessive Heat of Jun 26, 2021, when Portland International recorded high temperatures of 108, 112, and 116 F, breaking its previous all time record of 107.
That event recorded 93 deaths, and the text notes reports of "roads buckling due to heat" as cooling shelters were opened.
Earlier, on Jan 1, 2017, Cold/Wind Chill in your zone claimed four lives; the victims were homeless and died of hypothermia from exposure.
In January 2024, a Winter Storm brought blizzard-like conditions, at least 500 downed trees in the Portland Metro area, and a peak of 165,000 Portland General Electric customers without power.
Days later, an Ice Storm on Jan 16, 2024 left about one-half of an inch of ice, causing travel disruptions, power outages, and 4 known fatalities.

Heat returned in summer 2022, when the Multnomah County Medical Examiner reported suspected heat deaths and 10 requests for Emergency/Urgent care on the 30th, against a typical summer day of zero to one.
Heat events continued in 2023 and 2025, including Aug 14, 2023, when Multnomah County reported six suspected heat-related deaths, and Aug 10, 2025, when two fatalities were presumed heat related.
Across the county and nearby zones, the National Weather Service recorded 229 weather events since 2000, including 35 Heavy Snow, 35 Strong Wind and 16 Heat events.

SE-1158557.title: Winter Storm, Jan 12, 2024
SE-1158557.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-1158557.text: Winter Storm on Jan 12, 2024 in Greater Portland Metro Area (forecast zone ORZ006, YOUR zone: the address is inside it). Deaths: 9. Injuries: 16. Recorded damage: $10,250,000 (about $10.3 million).
SE-1158557.quote: Blizzard-like conditions were observed at the height of the storm with roughly 1 to 4 inches of a snow/sleet across the Portland and Vancouver metro area and widespread east wind gusts of 35-55 mph. This led to hundreds of downed trees and limbs, resulting in widespread and extended power outages. Multnomah County, the City of Portland, City of Lake Oswego declared a State of Emergency. Portland Parks and Recreation reported 380 downed trees or large branches, The City of Lake Oswego reported more than 100 downed trees. These reports along with trees downed on private property, at least 500 trees were downed in the Portland Metro area. Downed trees and power lines resulted in power outages. Portland General Electric had a peak count of 165,000 customers without power.

SE-1164391.title: Ice Storm, Jan 16, 2024
SE-1164391.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-1164391.text: Ice Storm on Jan 16, 2024 in Greater Portland Metro Area (forecast zone ORZ006, YOUR zone: the address is inside it). Deaths: 4. Injuries: 0. No damage figure was recorded.
SE-1164391.quote: About one-half of an inch of ice accumulation was inferred from the Portland ASOS, and across the Greater Portland Metro Area from the 16th to 17th. This resulted in travel disruptions, slip and fall injuries, and power outages. In addition to the ice, persistent freezing temperatures over several days led to frozen/burst water pipes and resulting damage to some homes and businesses. There were 4 known fatalities, 3 of which occurred when a tree branch fell, due to ice accumulation, on a power line which then fell on the car with 4 occupants. Three were electrocuted when they attempted to exit the vehicle. The fourth occupant was an 9 month old who survived.

SE-1046799.title: Excessive Heat, Jul 25, 2022
SE-1046799.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-1046799.text: Excessive Heat on Jul 25, 2022 in Greater Portland Metro Area (forecast zone ORZ006, YOUR zone: the address is inside it). Deaths: 12. Injuries: 0. No damage figure was recorded.
SE-1046799.quote: The Multnomah County Medical Examiner reported suspected deaths associated with the heat wave. One each on July 25th, 26th, 27th; two each on the 28th and 30th, all in Portland. A man drowned on the Sandy River on the 27th while paddle boarding. During the heatwave there were elevated numbers of heat related illnesses. For example on the 30th, Multnomah County reported 10 requests for Emergency/Urgent care. A typical summer day is zero to one. There was a cumulative of 63 heat illness, more than half of a typical summer. In another incident on July 25th, a man drowned while swimming at Henry Hagg Lake in Washington County. Also in Washington County, a dog died from the heat when left in a car. Other suspected heat related deaths occurred July 28th and 29th in Clackamas County.

SE-1136290.title: Excessive Heat, Aug 14, 2023
SE-1136290.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-1136290.text: Excessive Heat on Aug 14, 2023 in Greater Portland Metro Area (forecast zone ORZ006, YOUR zone: the address is inside it). Deaths: 5. Injuries: 0. No damage figure was recorded.
SE-1136290.quote: An extended period of hot weather lead to partner actions being taken and multiple heat related fatalities. High temperatures reached 101 to 108 in Portland between August 13 to 16. Low temperatures only fell to 68 to 73 on those days. Multnomah County reported six suspected heat-related deaths in Portland.

SE-1290018.title: Excessive Heat, Aug 10, 2025
SE-1290018.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-1290018.text: Excessive Heat on Aug 10, 2025 in Inner Portland Metro (forecast zone ORZ111, YOUR zone: the address is inside it). Deaths: 2. Injuries: 0. No damage figure was recorded.
SE-1290018.quote: There were two fatalities presumed heat related of a Male, 59 in the 97233 zip code and a Female, 58 in 97214 zip code. Emergency managers and health officials reported elevated Multnomah County 911 calls due to the heat and higher than normal hospital/urgent care heat related visits.

items.action: Your area logged record heat in June 2021, with Portland International reaching 112 and 116 F, and 41 days feeling like 100°F or more at your address since 2000. Identify cooling places such as libraries or shopping malls ahead of time.

why.label: Hottest day on record, Jun 28, 2021 (feels like 111.9°F)

guidance.text: Identify places in your community where you can go to get cool such as libraries and shopping malls or contact your local health department to find cooling options in your area.

items.action: The July 2024 heat in your area had overnight lows well into the 60s, with little cooling for those without air conditioning. Do not rely on a fan as your primary cooling device, and check on older adults and neighbors.

guidance.text: Do not rely on a fan as your primary cooling device. Fans create air flow and a false sense of comfort, but do not reduce body temperature or prevent heat-related illnesses.
Check on family members, older adults and neighbors.

items.action: The January 2024 ice storm in your area left about one-half of an inch of ice, with travel disruptions and power outages. Stay off roads if at all possible, and if trapped in your car, stay inside.

guidance.text: Stay off roads if at all possible. If trapped in your car, then stay inside.

items.action: The January 2024 winter storm brought east wind gusts of 35-55 mph and widespread, extended power outages in your area. If you use a generator, run it only outdoors and away from windows, and keep freezers and refrigerators closed.

guidance.text: Use a generator, but ONLY outdoors and away from windows.

items.action: A December 2014 high wind event in your area downed several trees, closed roads and killed one person when a tree fell on a moving car. Cut down or trim trees that may be in danger of falling on your home.

guidance.text: Cut down or trim trees that may be in danger of falling on your home.

items.action: An EF0 tornado on Jul 1, 2019 passed 5.5 km from your address, uprooting trees and tearing shingles off roofs. Sign up for your community's warning system, and in a tornado warning go to a basement, safe room or interior room away from windows.

guidance.text: Sign up for your community’s warning system. The Emergency Alert System (EAS) and NOAA Weather Radio also provide emergency alerts. If your community has sirens, become familiar with the warning tone.

guidance.source: National Weather Service, What to do during a tornado
guidance.text: At Your House: If you are in a tornado warning, go to your basement, safe room, or an interior room away from windows. Don't forget pets if time allows.
